idea-plugin.name: Bisotun Flow Extractor
idea-plugin.description:
Instantly Extract Execution Call Flows & Data Models

Bisotun Flow Extractor automates code navigation by tracing and extracting nested execution call hierarchies and related data models directly to your clipboard in clean Markdown format—ideal for context injection into LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Ollama) or team documentation.

Why "Bisotun"? The Philosophy Beneath the Name

The plugin is named after Mount Bisotun, a majestic peak located near Kermanshah, Iran, famous for holding the world's largest limestone cliff and the historic Bisotun Inscription—carved in three ancient cuneiform languages (Old Persian, Elamite, and Babylonian) by command of Darius the Great.

Just as Mount Bisotun is structured in magnificent, enduring geological layers, complex software code is also built layer upon layer. Bisotun Flow Extractor dives deep through these architectural layers to unearth, decode, and document your call flows and data models with historical precision.

Key Features:

  • Deep Flow Extraction: Recursively crawls method execution call chains up to configurable depths.
  • Model Crawler: Automatically extracts referenced DTOs, Entities, and Interfaces.
  • Multi-Language Support: Support for Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript (including React JSX/TSX), C++ (.cpp, .cc, .cxx, .h, .hh, .hpp, .hxx) and Go (.go). Go support requires GoLand (or IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate) with the bundled Go plugin enabled, because it is built on native Go PSI.
  • LLM-Optimized Markdown: Generates structured markdown trees ready to be pasted into AI prompts.

Shortcuts:

  • Ctrl + Alt + Shift + D : Copy Deep Flow (Calls + Models)
  • Ctrl + Alt + Shift + S : Copy Shallow Flow (Calls + Models)
  • Ctrl + Alt + Shift + M : Copy Shallow Flow (No Models)
  • Ctrl + Alt + Shift + C : Copy Method Only
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0

  • Go extraction now uses native Go PSI from the official JetBrains Go plugin instead of a bounded tokenizer. Declarations, types, generics, signatures, receivers, local variables and call targets are read from the Go PSI model, and calls are resolved with JetBrains reference resolution across files and imported project packages.
  • Go requires GoLand (or IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate) with the bundled Go plugin enabled. IntelliJ IDEA Community alone does not provide the Go PSI APIs, so Go extraction reports that prerequisite instead of falling back to text parsing. Other languages keep working where their plugins/PSI are available.
  • The plugin now builds against IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate 2024.1 with the Go plugin dependency and is verified against GoLand 2024.1.4, 2024.2 and 2024.3.
  • Java and Go PSI are loaded from optional content modules (bisotun-java, bisotun-go), so IDEs without the Java or Go plugin do not load those classes.
  • Go interface calls stay at the interface declaration; dynamic or unresolved targets are reported as unresolved and are never matched by name.

1.0.9

  • Added Go flow extraction for .go files: packages and imports (including aliases), structs, interfaces, embedded types, fields, functions with multiple return values, pointer and value receivers, generics, local and short declarations, project-local models, control-flow statements and nested calls.
  • Go calls resolve across files of the same package and into project-local imported packages (resolved through go.mod). Unknown receiver types and interface implementations stay unresolved instead of being guessed, and built-in/standard-library noise is filtered.
  • Go uses a bounded tokenizer because the JetBrains Go plugin is not part of the IntelliJ IDEA Community SDK this plugin targets; the copied output states that limitation.

1.0.8

  • Fixed C++ resolution across .cpp/.hpp boundaries: same-file methods defined later, header prototypes with source definitions, template members such as Repository<T>::filter, and receiver calls through known fields including smart pointers.
  • Lambda predicate/comparator bodies are nested callbacks of the containing call instead of duplicate top-level flow steps; standard-library noise such as error.what() is filtered, and quoted includes are no longer treated as executable steps.

1.0.7

  • Migrated the flow dispatcher to the non-deprecated Application.runReadAction(Computable) API, rethrowing ProcessCanceledException instead of swallowing it.
  • Renamed the optional Java descriptor java-part.xml to bisotun-java.xml and updated the config-file references in the optional dependencies.

1.0.6

  • Maintenance release: Fully resolved all plugin verifier warnings to ensure seamless IDE compatibility.
  • Migrated deprecated ReadAction.compute calls to the modern runReadAction standard.
  • Optimized optional dependency configuration (config-file declaration) per JetBrains Platform best practices.

1.0.5

  • Added robust multi-language flow extraction support for Python (`.py`, `pyw`, `pyi`) with full absolute/relative import resolution.
  • Resolved IntelliJ IDEA module classloader constraints via optional Java dependencies, enabling seamless multi-IDE compatibility (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm).

1.0.4

  • Added inline animated GIF demo inside the plugin description for direct viewing in IntelliJ IDEA client.

1.0.3

  • Added official branded plugin icon and visual assets.
  • Enhanced plugin description with the historical and architectural philosophy of Mount Bisotun.

1.0.2

  • Added full flow extraction support for JS, JSX, TS, and TSX files in IntelliJ Community.
  • Refactored architecture into a unified dispatcher strategy for improved stability.
